Mayor Brett Smiley Announces Two New Grant Programs to Support Providence’s Cultural Venues and Festivals  
            PROVIDENCE, RI – Mayor Brett P. Smiley and the Department of Art, Culture and Tourism (ACT) today announced two new grant programs to improve Providence’s cultural facilities and support festivals that celebrate the city’s diverse communities. The Cultural Facilities Improvement Grants program will provide $700,000 over two years for improvements to public arts venues, while the Cultural Festival Grant Fund will provide $50,000 for cultural festivals during fiscal year 2027.

“Providence’s artists and cultural organizations give neighbors countless opportunities to experience art, learn something new and celebrate their heritage,” said Mayor Brett Smiley. “These grants will help organizations improve the spaces that make that work possible and support cultural festivals that bring our neighborhoods together.”

Both programs will be administered by ACT, with funding available for facility repairs and enhancements as well as established, free public cultural festivals.

Mayor Brett Smiley Accepting Nominations for MLK Hall of Fame  
            The City of Providence is now accepting nominations for its twenty-third annual Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Hall of Fame induction ceremony. Individuals inducted to the MLK Hall of Fame are civic leaders that support the legacy of Dr. King and embody his work here in Providence.

“Dr. King’s legacy lives on through people who choose to serve their neighbors, stand up for justice and strengthen their communities each and every day,” said Mayor Brett Smiley. “Providence is proud and grateful to have so many residents and leaders who embody each of these values through their tireless work and dedicated service to others. I look forward to recognizing those who have helped make Providence the inclusive, welcoming city we all know and cherish.”

Letters of nomination will be accepted beginning today until November 30. Nominees must be a resident of Providence or have accomplished a significant amount of community work in Providence. Letters should be no more than two pages long and specify how the nominee exemplifies the spirit of Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s commitment to equity, civil rights and justice.

City of Providence Announces Winter Rates for Providence Community Electricity Program
            Today, the City of Providence announced new winter electricity supply prices for the Providence Community Electricity program to go into effect beginning with the November 2026 meter read. The program’s winter pricing for the default electricity will cost less than RI Energy’s Residential Last Resort Service rate, while continuing to offer 5% more clean energy from RI based sources. The new prices will be fixed for six months through customers’ April 2027 meter read. Current participants do not need to take any action to remain in the program and receive the new pricing for the product in which they are currently enrolled.

Mayor Brett Smiley, FirstWorks Kick Off PVDFest 2026
            PROVIDENCE, RI – Mayor Brett P. Smiley, Councilman John Goncalves, founding producing partner FirstWorks Executive Artistic Director Kathleen Pletcher, President of Real Access Motivates Progress (RAMP) Tina Guenette, and Department of Art, Culture and Tourism Director Joe Wilson Jr. today kicked off PVDFest 2026, Providence’s signature celebration of art, culture and community.


Programming begins Thursday, September 17 with a free skating party at the Providence Rink, followed by the main festival on Friday, September 18 from 5 to 10 pm and Saturday, September 19 from noon to 10 pm.


PVDFest will fill Downtown Providence with live music, dance, public art, maker spaces, artisan markets, food, skating and activities celebrating the cultures and creative communities that make Providence the Creative Capital. This year’s footprint includes Kennedy Plaza, the Providence Rink, Burnside Park and the streets surrounding City Hall.
